title: Adjust activities that worsen your discomfort
description: Consider shortening, changing, or easing back on an activity that clearly makes your shoulder feel worse. Avoid complete rest; keep to comfortable everyday movement.
whenItMayHelp: For non-urgent shoulder discomfort when particular tasks or movements are aggravating symptoms.
precautions: Do not use this advice to delay assessment after a significant injury or when pain is severe, worsening, or movement is very limited. This is not an exercise plan.

verification.reviewNotes: Checked the NHS Trust page for activity modification, avoiding complete rest, and urgent assessment advice. No exercise prescription was taken from this source.

title: Try a pillow to support your arm while sleeping
description: A pillow may help support your arm while you sleep or keep you from rolling onto the painful side.
whenItMayHelp: When a supported position feels more comfortable during rest or sleep.
precautions: Use a position only if it feels comfortable. Get medical assessment for a significant injury, severe symptoms, or major difficulty moving the arm.

verification.reviewNotes: Checked the NHS Trust page for sleeping positions and pillow support. The page also advises seeking assessment for significant injury or serious symptoms.

title: Consider a wrapped heat or cold pack
description: Some people find a heat or cold pack soothing for shoulder discomfort. Put a cloth between the pack and your skin; do not place it directly on bare skin.
whenItMayHelp: As a temporary comfort measure for non-urgent shoulder pain. People may prefer warmth or coolness differently.
precautions: Stop if it feels uncomfortable. Do not use this instead of medical assessment after a significant injury or for severe or worsening symptoms.

verification.reviewNotes: The NHS Trust page says heat or ice may ease pain and cautions against applying them to bare skin. It does not claim either option is right for everyone.

title: Ask a pharmacist about non-prescription pain relief
description: If you are considering a non-prescription pain medicine, ask a pharmacist or healthcare professional what may be suitable for you. Tell them about your health conditions and all prescription, non-prescription, and natural health products you use.
whenItMayHelp: If you are unsure what option is suitable, especially if you are an older adult, take other medicines, or have a health condition.
precautions: This guide does not choose a medicine or provide a dose. Follow the product label and advice from your healthcare professional; check before combining products.

verification.reviewNotes: Checked the NHS Trust recommendation to ask a pharmacist or GP about simple pain relief and Health Canada medication-safety guidance on risks, directions, and interactions. No medicine or dose is recommended here.
